title: Before 2017, Language AI Read One Word at a Time

panels.prompt: A vast dark infinite library stretching into darkness, endless shelves packed with books in every language, a tiny lone figure sits at a desk reading a book through a narrow cone of flashlight illuminating only one word at a time, the rest of the page and library swallowed in deep shadow, moody and atmospheric, sense of immense knowledge just out of reach, Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, deep navy and indigo tones with a single warm yellow spotlight cone

panels.text: In Issue 6, we watched neural networks learn to see. They could look at a photograph and say "that's a cat." Vision was conquered. But language? Language was a different beast.

panels.prompt: A small cute flat rectangular robot made of old punch-card paper, folded origami-style with dot-matrix eyes glowing amber, holding a tiny scroll that trails behind it showing fading words, sitting on a stack of old computer manuals, one stubby paper-fold arm pointing at fading text behind it, looking slightly frustrated. A white speech bubble with black outline near the top. Inside the bubble the text reads: "RNNs read one word at a time. Left to right." Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, warm paper-tone background with blue #4A9BD9 accents
panels.bubble_text: RNNs read one word at a time. Left to right.
panels.speaker: TAPE

panels.text: Each word updated a small bundle of numbers called a hidden state -- the model's attempt to remember everything it had read so far. Like rewriting a summary after every chapter. By chapter 20, the details from chapter 1 have faded.

panels.prompt: The same vast infinite library but now transformed: every book is open, every word glowing with golden light, brilliant golden threads of light connecting related words across different books and different shelves, the entire room radiating with interconnected knowledge, a web of luminous connections spanning the whole space, breathtaking transformation from darkness to radiance, Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, warm golden tones with blue #4A9BD9 thread highlights

A small cute round brass robot with big wide curious green clock-face eyes, a single gear on its back and a tiny top hat, standing in the glowing golden library looking up in awe with stubby arms spread wide, bright golden threads of light reflecting in its eyes, excited body language. A white speech bubble with black outline near the top. Inside the bubble the text reads: "Then eight researchers changed everything." Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, golden and blue tones
panels.speaker: CLOCKWORK

panels.prompt: Close-up of two glowing words 'it' and 'cat' floating in dark space, connected by a bright luminous blue thread labeled 'attention' in small clean white text, the thread pulses with energy like a fiber optic cable, surrounding dimmer threads connect to other faded words in the background, a date stamp 'June 12, 2017' glows in the bottom corner, Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, deep navy background with bright blue #4A9BD9 thread

panels.text: An improvement called LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory, 1997) added special "gates" to choose what to remember and forget. But the fundamental problem remained: one word at a time, everything compressed into a fixed-size memory, and no way to go back.

panels.caption: RNNs process one word at a time -- memory degrades. Self-attention connects every word directly.

panels.text: RNNs read language like someone peering through a keyhole -- one word at a time, trying to remember everything on a tiny scrap of memory. The model could not go back. It could not look ahead. And the longer the text, the more old information degraded.
In June 2017, eight researchers at Google would propose a radical answer: throw away the entire sequential machinery. Let every word see every other word, all at once.
